Quen 1.5-0.5B [Bai等人,2023] 从其现成的预先训练的检查站(Quen/Quen1.5-0.5B)装入,是一个密集的变形器,带有SwiGLU MLP激活,RoPE位置嵌入,以及多头注意(24层;隐藏大小1,024;MLP中间尺寸2,816;16个查询头和16个关键值头).
我们评价了所有24层的两个目标。 首先,MLP神经元去除无偏差的行_proj和gate_proj矩阵和列的无偏差的下_proj矩阵(最大 QQ活动 = 0.0\max\text{活动 = 0.0;在 k = 0.5 k= 0.5 中去除33.7%的非嵌入参数). 第二,注意头清除零 Q, K K, V V 投影行(及其添加偏差)和选定头的无偏差 O 投影列(最大 Q 活动 = 0.0\max = text{活动 = 0.0;在 k = 0.5 k= 0.5 时删除16.3%的非嵌入参数).
这两个目标在颗粒度上有所不同:每层包含2,816 2{,}816 MLP神经元(5,504 5{,}504 in Quen 1.8B),但只有16个注意头. 由于注意力减退可以移除每层16 k \ llode 16\,k\rlode整体头部,因此被移除的头部分数在1 / 16 1/16(6.25% 6.25\)的步数中增加,在16 k 16\,k不是整数时略低于k k(例如,k = 0.3 k = 0.3去除16头中的4 4个,或25\ 25%头部和8.2%的无嵌入参数). 为计算离散头数和路径参数大小,补充图9和补充表6的图案和与 k 和去除的非嵌入参数的准确部分相对应的降解曲线。

blocks.en:
Qwen 1.5-1.8B [ Bai et al., 2023 ] is likewise loaded from its off-the-shelf pretrained checkpoint ( Qwen/Qwen1.5-1.8B ); it shares the architecture family and depth of the 0.5B model (24 layers; 16 query and 16 key–value heads) but is wider, with hidden size 2,048 and MLP intermediate size 5,504.
It follows the same ablation protocol as Qwen 0.5B, removing 33.4% of non-embedding parameters at k = 0.5 k=0.5 for MLP ablation and 16.6% for attention-head ablation.
blocks.zh:
Quen 1.5-1.8B[Bai等人,2023]同样从其现成的预先训练的检查站(Quen/Quen1.5-1.8B)装入;它共享0.5B型号(24层;16个查询和16个钥匙-值头)的建筑家族和深度,但范围更广,隐藏大小为2 048,MLP中间尺寸为5 504。
它遵循与Qwen 0.5B相同的衰减协议,在K=0.5k=0.5时取消了33.4%的非嵌入参数,在MLP衰减时取消了16.6%的注意力头衰减.

blocks.en: Ablation, Fine-Tuning, and Plasticity Sensitivity Protocol
blocks.zh: 减容、微调和可塑性敏感性议定书

blocks.en: For each model–target combination and ablation fraction k ∈ { 0.0 , 0.1 , 0.2 , … , 0.9 } k\in\{0.0,0.1,0.2,\ldots,0.9\} , we run 5 independent trials across the full sweep to support all main and supplementary degradation curves (Supplementary Tables 5 – 16 ). We increase replication to 15 independent trials per k k across the shared transition region k ∈ { 0.1 , 0.2 , 0.3 , 0.4 } k\in\{0.1,0.2,0.3,0.4\} ( n = 60 n=60 trials per pathway) for the Qwen null-model pathway tests in Section 2.3 and Supplement S3 . For the Cloze, Brysbaert word-concreteness [ Brysbaert et al., 2014 ] , and Philadelphia Naming Test (PNT) [ Mirman et al., 2010 ] analyses (Section 2.5 ; Supplements S7 – S8 ), we evaluate 10 independent trials at k = 0.2 k=0.2 , alongside the deterministic greedy baseline at k = 0.0 k=0.0 and 5 trials at k ∈ { 0.1 , 0.3 , … , 0.9 } k\in\{0.1,0.3,\ldots,0.9\} . Each trial proceeds in five steps:

blocks.en: 1. Deep copy the pretrained model and seed all random number generators deterministically per ( k , trial ) (k,\text{trial}) . 2. Ablate : randomly select ⌊ k × n ⌋ \lfloor k\times n\rfloor target units per layer independently across layers and zero all associated weights and gate/head biases across all layers (systemic ablation). 3. Freeze ablated weights at zero during fine-tuning (via gradient hooks and post-update masking) so that silenced units or pruned connections cannot recover. 4. Fine-tune briefly at every k ∈ { 0.0 , 0.1 , … , 0.9 } k\in\{0.0,0.1,\ldots,0.9\} (so undamaged k = 0 k=0 and damaged k > 0 k>0 models undergo the exact same adaptation step) as a simple proxy for local compensatory plasticity (primary weak SGD arm): • LSTM-based models use SGD ( lr = 10 − 3 \mathrm{lr}=10^{-3} , gradient clipping 0.25, bptt = 70 \mathrm{bptt}=70 ) on TinyStories for 40 sequence steps (Small LSTM, plain lowercased tokens) or 50 sequence steps (AWD-LSTM, with fastai xxbos / xxmaj / xxup markers). • Qwen models use SGD ( lr = 10 − 3 \mathrm{lr}=10^{-3} ) across the first 500 TinyStories passages (passages 1–500, max sequence length 64), clipping gradients to 0.25 after each passage’s backward pass and accumulating over 8 passages per update (62 weight updates in total). Because 40–50 steps of clipped SGD at lr = 10 − 3 \mathrm{lr}=10^{-3} on out-of-domain TinyStories move the LSTM weights by only ‖ Δ ​ θ ‖ 2 ≤ 0.012 \|\Delta\theta\|_{2}\leq 0.012 (relative change ∼ 10 − 5 {\sim}10^{-5} ), this step leaves LSTM WikiText-2 accuracy essentially unchanged. Thus, the weak and none arms coincide for the LSTMs, whereas 500 steps of AdamW on the same TinyStories passages in the strong arm do shift WikiText-2 accuracy (Supplement S9 ). 5. Evaluate on the held-out test set.

blocks.en: Evaluate on the held-out test set.
blocks.zh: 评估暂停测试

blocks.en:
Because biological recovery after acute damage operates through local weight adjustments rather than global network retraining, we use brief fixed-step SGD without momentum ( weak arm) as our primary protocol.
To test whether the contrast between Transformer and LSTM curve shapes depends on this choice, we compare zero fine-tuning ( none ), brief local SGD ( weak ), and 500-step AdamW retraining ( strong , plus in-domain WikiText-103 strong_wt103 for both LSTMs) across k ∈ { 0.0 , 0.1 , … , 0.9 } k\in\{0.0,0.1,\ldots,0.9\} . This comparison covers both recurrent architectures across all three ablation modes and the pretrained Transformers (Qwen 0.5B across both pathways, plus Qwen 1.8B MLP across none , weak , and k ≤ 0.2 k\leq 0.2 of strong ).
With zero fine-tuning, Qwen MLP ablation still exhibits a sharp late threshold collapse without an early retention advantage over the LSTMs. Conversely, the Small LSTM and AWD-LSTM whole-unit and recurrent pathways decline smoothly without a cliff even under 500 steps of in-domain AdamW retraining (Supplement S9 ; Supplementary Figures 14 – 16 ).
blocks.zh:
因为急性损伤后的生物恢复是通过局部重量调整而不是通过全球网络再培训进行,所以我们使用没有动力(弱臂)的短暂固定步骤SGD作为我们的主要协议.
为了测试变形器和LSTM曲线形状的对比是否取决于这个选择,我们比较了零微调(无),短暂的本地SGD(弱),以及500步的AdamW再培训(强,加域内WikiText-103 strong_wt103,双LSTMs),横跨 k_{ { 0.0, 0.1,0.9} k\in_ 0.0,0.1,\ldots,0.9}. 这种比较既包括所有三种衰减模式的经常性结构,也包括经过预先训练的变形器(两个路径的Quen 0.5B,加上Wen 1.8B MLP,不分强弱的)和k 0.2 k\leq 0.2。
在零微调的情况下,Quen MLP的膨胀仍然显示出尖锐的晚期阈值崩溃,没有比LSTMs早期的保留优势. 与此相反,小型LSTM和AWD-LSTM的全单元和经常性通道在没有悬崖的情况下顺利下降,甚至不到500步的AdamW域内再培训(补充S9;补充图14-16)。

blocks.en:
For accuracy evaluation, LSTM models are tested on WikiText-2 [ Merity et al., 2017 ] ( 241,200 241{,}200 lowercased lexical tokens for the Small LSTM; 271,480 271{,}480 tokens for the AWD-LSTM, comprising 241,202 241{,}202 lexical tokens and 30,278 30{,}278 unscored xxbos / xxmaj / xxup prefix markers). Excluding out-of-vocabulary xxunk targets yields 225,702 225{,}702 scored in-vocabulary tokens for the Small LSTM and 225,704 225{,}704 for the AWD-LSTM. Qwen models are tested on the first 32 tokens of each held-out TinyStories passage (passages 501–1,000, yielding up to 31 next-token predictions per passage, or 15,268 15{,}268 scored targets in total). The passages used to rank tokens for the auxiliary Qwen spectral analysis (passages 1–2,000; Supplement S4 ) overlap these evaluation passages.
To ensure cross-architecture comparability, we report relative accuracy ( Acc ⁡ ( k ) / Acc ⁡ ( 0 ) \mathrm{Acc}(k)/\mathrm{Acc}(0) ), evaluate error distributions against an accuracy-matched random-failure baseline, and base all clinical parallel assignments (Section 2.5 ) on the shared 100-prompt Cloze battery.

blocks.en:
Next-word prediction accuracy (top-1) is evaluated over all valid in-vocabulary test tokens and reported as relative accuracy RelAcc ⁡ ( k ) = Acc ⁡ ( k ) / Acc ⁡ ( 0 ) \mathrm{RelAcc}(k)=\mathrm{Acc}(k)/\mathrm{Acc}(0) , with bootstrap standard errors across trials. For both LSTMs, out-of-vocabulary ( xxunk ) targets are excluded from scoring. For the AWD-LSTM, fastai formatting tokens ( xxbos , xxmaj , xxup ) are also excluded from target scoring; however, because they remain in the input sequence and indicate whether the following word is capitalized, they contribute to the AWD-LSTM’s higher baseline accuracy relative to the Small LSTM.
To test whether each degradation curve follows a straight line or bends non-linearly, we fit both a 2-parameter line y ⁡ ( x ) = a + b ​ x y(x)=a+bx and a 3-parameter logistic S-curve y ⁡ ( x ) = a / ( 1 + exp ⁡ ( b ⁡ ( x − x 0 ) ) ) y(x)=a/(1+\exp(b(x-x_{0}))) to the trial-level relative accuracy points. We perform these fits against both x = k x=k and x = fraction of non-embedding parameters removed x=\text{fraction of non-embedding parameters removed} , comparing them via Δ ​ AIC = AIC logistic − AIC linear \Delta\mathrm{AIC}=\mathrm{AIC}_{\mathrm{logistic}}-\mathrm{AIC}_{\mathrm{linear}} (Supplementary Table 6 ). A Δ ​ AIC < − 2 \Delta\mathrm{AIC}<-2 indicates non-linear curvature, while the presence of an early buffered plateau versus an immediate drop is assessed from surviving relative accuracy across k ∈ [ 0.1 , 0.3 ] k\in[0.1,0.3] . By this criterion, only attention-head ablation shows an early plateau. Because Qwen MLP relative accuracy at k = 0.1 ​ – ​ 0.2 k=0.1\text{--}0.2 is not systematically higher than that of the LSTMs ( 71 % ​ – ​ 94 % 71\%\text{--}94\% of baseline across k = 0.1 ​ – ​ 0.2 k=0.1\text{--}0.2 in Qwen MLP vs. 75 % ​ – ​ 93 % 75\%\text{--}93\% in the LSTMs; Supplementary Table 6 ), we describe the MLP curves as a late threshold collapse.

blocks.en:
We use 100 sentence prompts with predictable final words, stratified by POS tag (48 nouns, 25 verbs, 22 adjectives, 5 adverbs).
Each prompt is fed to the model and the top-1 predicted word is extracted. For the LSTMs, we skip fastai control tokens ( xxunk , xxmaj , xxup , xxbos , xxeos , xxfld , xxpad , xxrep , xxwrep ) when selecting the top lexical prediction; for Qwen, we strip leading and trailing whitespace from the decoded subword token.
Part-of-speech (POS) tags are assigned using NLTK’s [ Bird et al., 2009 ] standard POS tagger (Universal tagset), applied to the predicted word on its own rather than in sentence context. Prompts whose predicted token remains a non-word symbol are scored as POS mismatches and assigned zero semantic similarity. Semantic similarity is also set to zero whenever the predicted word’s tag is not a content-word tag, even if the word has a GloVe vector, which couples the semantic score to the syntactic score.
For content-tagged predictions, semantic similarity is the cosine similarity between 50-dimensional GloVe [ Pennington et al., 2014 ] vectors ( glove.6B.50d ) of the predicted and target words; out-of-vocabulary predictions receive similarity 0.0.
Across k ∈ { 0.0 , 0.2 } k\in\{0.0,0.2\} , we evaluate 10 independent trials ( N = 1,000 N=1{,}000 prompt evaluations per condition). We use these to compute 95% confidence intervals and two-sided permutation tests ( 20,000 20{,}000 permutations, with Holm correction across the planned contrasts) for the Brysbaert concreteness shift Δ ​ Conc. \Delta\text{Conc.} (Supplement S7 ) and the Philadelphia Naming Test (PNT) error proportions (Supplement S8 ).
blocks.zh:
我们使用100句提示,带有可预测的最终词,由POS标记分级(48个名词,25个动词,22个形容词,5个副词).
每个提示输入到模型中,并提取出前1预测的单词. 对于 LSTM ,我们在选择顶级词典预测时跳过 fastai 控制符( xxunk, xxmaj , xxup , xxbos, xxeos, xxfld , xxpad, xxrep , xxwrep ) ; 对于 Quen, 我们从解码的子词符号中跳过引导和跟踪的白空间.
部分语义(POS)标记使用NLTK的[Bird et al.,2009]标准POS标记器(Universal tagset)进行分配,应用到预言词本身而不是句子上下文中. 其预言符号仍为非单词符号的提示被评为POS不匹配并指定为零语义相似性. 语义相似性也设定为0,只要预言词的标记不是内容词标记,即使该词有一个GloVe矢量,而该矢量将语义分数与合成分数相配.
对于标注内容的预测,语义相似性是预测词和目标词的50维GloVe[Pennington等人,2014年]矢量(手套6B.50d)的同位素相似性;省外预测得到相似性0.0.
透过k { 0.0, 0.2} k\ in\ 0.0, 0.2 } 我们评价 10 个独立审判( N = 1000 N = 1{,} 000 迅速评价每个条件) 。 我们用这些来计算95%的置信间隔和双侧穿透测试(20,000 20{,}000 个穿透计划对比度的Holm校正),用于Brysbaert混凝土变换 QQ Conc.\Delta\text{Conc.}(补充 S7)和费城命名测试(PNT)错误比例(补充 S8).

blocks.en: Across the six main-paper unit-level conditions and the four supplementary LSTM connection-pruning controls, next-word prediction accuracy evolves as follows: • Small LSTM (baseline 27.5%): Under whole-unit removal ( weight_ih + weight_hh + gate biases, main paper Figure 2 a), next-token accuracy degrades smoothly and monotonically across the entire range without an initial plateau: 25.5% at k = 0.1 k=0.1 ( RelAcc = 0.927 \mathrm{RelAcc}=0.927 ), 22.6% at k = 0.2 k=0.2 ( 0.822 0.822 ), 19.3% at k = 0.3 k=0.3 ( 0.702 0.702 ), 15.7% at k = 0.4 k=0.4 ( 0.570 0.570 ), 12.6% at k = 0.5 k=0.5 ( 0.458 0.458 ), 10.9% at k = 0.6 k=0.6 ( 0.398 0.398 ), 9.5% at k = 0.7 k=0.7 ( 0.344 0.344 ), 7.5% at k = 0.8 k=0.8 ( 0.274 0.274 ), and 7.12% at k = 0.9 k=0.9 ( 0.259 0.259 , where all five trials settle on always guessing the single most common word in the text, “the” , which makes up 7.12% of test tokens; Table 8 ). Dissecting the two incoming pathways separately in our supplementary controls (Figure 8 , row 1) shows why: hidden-state ( weight_hh ) pruning alone tracks whole-unit removal closely through k = 0.3 k=0.3 and degrades more gradually thereafter because unit j j remains driven by the current input word x t x_{t} via weight_ih (25.2% at k = 0.1 k=0.1 , 21.3% at k = 0.2 k=0.2 , 15.9% at k = 0.5 k=0.5 , and 13.3% at k = 0.9 k=0.9 , preserving 48.3% of baseline accuracy at extreme ablation). When plotted against the fraction of non-embedding parameters removed, this trajectory is nearly a straight line with slope − 1.02 -1.02 and the smallest departure from linearity of any condition ( Δ ​ AIC = − 7.75 \Delta\mathrm{AIC}=-7.75 ; Figure 9 and Table 6 ). Conversely, input-projection ( weight_ih ) pruning alone produces a steep initial collapse: accuracy drops to 17.9% at k = 0.1 k=0.1 and 3.8% at k = 0.2 k=0.2 , then remains at a near-zero floor between 1.6–3.3% for k ≥ 0.3 k\geq 0.3 (e.g., 1.6% at k = 0.5 k=0.5 , 1.8% at k = 0.8 k=0.8 , and 1.7% at k = 0.9 k=0.9 ). • AWD-LSTM (baseline 38.1%): Under whole-unit removal ( weight_ih + weight_hh + gate biases, main paper Figure 2 b), next-token accuracy likewise degrades smoothly and near-monotonically (apart from a floor at k ≥ 0.8 k\geq 0.8 ) without a buffered plateau: 34.1% at k = 0.1 k=0.1 ( RelAcc = 0.896 \mathrm{RelAcc}=0.896 ), 28.7% at k = 0.2 k=0.2 ( 0.753 0.753 ), 23.0% at k = 0.3 k=0.3 ( 0.603 0.603 ), 17.3% at k = 0.4 k=0.4 ( 0.455 0.455 ), 13.1% at k = 0.5 k=0.5 ( 0.344 0.344 ), 10.0% at k = 0.6 k=0.6 ( 0.264 0.264 ), 7.6% at k = 0.7 k=0.7 ( 0.201 0.201 ), 6.5% at k = 0.8 k=0.8 ( 0.171 0.171 ), and 6.8% at k = 0.9 k=0.9 ( 0.178 0.178 ; Table 7 ). In the supplementary pathway-connection controls (Figure 8 , row 2), hidden-state ( weight_hh ) pruning degrades gradually from 36.0% at k = 0.1 k=0.1 and 33.0% at k = 0.2 k=0.2 to 21.9% at k = 0.5 k=0.5 (57.6% of baseline) and 13.4% at k = 0.9 k=0.9 (35.1% of baseline, closely matching the Small LSTM recurrent pathway’s 58.0% relative accuracy at k = 0.5 k=0.5 ; Table 9 ), whereas input-projection ( weight_ih ) pruning drops steeply from 27.7% at k = 0.2 k=0.2 and 18.5% at k = 0.3 k=0.3 to 9.7% at k = 0.4 k=0.4 , 5.7% at k = 0.5 k=0.5 , and 1.5–2.2% for k ≥ 0.6 k\geq 0.6 (Table 10 ). • Qwen 0.5B (baseline 53.6%): MLP neuron ablation exhibits a late threshold collapse: accuracy is 89.3% of baseline at k = 0.1 k=0.1 (47.9%) and 70.6% at k = 0.2 k=0.2 (37.9%), then collapses sharply between k = 0.3 k=0.3 (30.4%) and k = 0.4 k=0.4 (13.8%), reaching 4.2% at k = 0.5 k=0.5 and near zero ( ≈ 1 % {\approx}1\% ) for k ≥ 0.7 k\geq 0.7 . R_{4}(\mathrm{abl})=\frac{\left(\sum_{i}i^{4}\frac{\alpha e_{i}}{\alpha\sum_{j}e_{j}}\right)^{1/4}}{\left(\sum_{i}i^{2}\frac{\alpha e_{i}}{\alpha\sum_{j}e_{j}}\right)^{1/2}}=R_{4}(\mathrm{base})\,. (6) Raw R 4 R_{4} rises as accuracy falls because an undamaged model mostly gets common, low-index words right and misses harder words; as damage increases and the model misses many common words, the average error index in the denominator ( μ 2 1 / 2 \mu_{2}^{1/2} ) drops faster than the extreme tail in the numerator ( μ 4 1 / 4 \mu_{4}^{1/4} ), pushing R 4 R_{4} upward.

blocks.en: The Fourier spectral metrics β \beta and G G track how smoothly prediction errors vary across word-frequency ranks as ablation increases (Figures 11 and 12 ; Tables 7 – 16 ). They also show why accuracy-matched null correction (Section 2.3 ) is needed when comparing pathways.
blocks.zh: Fourier光谱测量仪β\beta和G跟踪预测误差是如何随着衰减增加而随词频级而变化的(图11和12;表7 – 16)。 它们也表明为什么在比较路径时需要精确对应的无效修正(第2.3节)。

blocks.en: Both LSTMs start with steep baseline spectra ( β = − 1.37 \beta=-1.37 , G = 3.71 G=3.71 for the Small LSTM; β = − 1.53 \beta=-1.53 , G = 3.31 G=3.31 for the AWD-LSTM). Under whole-unit removal (Figure 11 , top row; Tables 7 – 8 ), the Small LSTM spectrum changes little across mild-to-moderate damage ( β \beta between − 1.37 -1.37 and − 1.22 -1.22 , G G between 3.65 3.65 and 3.96 3.96 for k ∈ [ 0 , 0.5 ] k\in[0,0.5] ), steepens to β = − 1.54 \beta=-1.54 and G = 4.74 G=4.74 at k = 0.7 k=0.7 , and settles at β = − 1.29 \beta=-1.29 and G = 3.89 G=3.89 at k = 0.9 k=0.9 . In the AWD-LSTM, whole-unit removal produces a non-monotonic curve: β \beta first flattens from − 1.53 -1.53 ( G = 3.31 G=3.31 ) at k = 0 k=0 to − 1.14 -1.14 ( G = 3.45 G=3.45 ) at k = 0.4 k=0.4 , then steepens sharply at k = 0.6 k=0.6 ( β = − 2.06 \beta=-2.06 , G = 5.83 G=5.83 ) as Cloze output collapses, and finally moves back toward β = − 1.43 \beta=-1.43 and G = 4.33 G=4.33 at k = 0.9 k=0.9 .

In the supplementary LSTM connection-pruning controls (Figure 12 , top two rows; Tables 9 – 12 ), recurrent-connection ( weight_hh ) pruning in the AWD-LSTM flattens the spectrum slightly at mild damage ( β = − 1.39 \beta=-1.39 , G = 3.16 G=3.16 at k = 0.2 k=0.2 ) before steepening steadily to β = − 1.73 \beta=-1.73 and G = 5.13 G=5.13 at k = 0.9 k=0.9 . Small LSTM weight_hh pruning follows a similar path, moving from β = − 1.09 \beta=-1.09 and G = 2.95 G=2.95 at k = 0.3 k=0.3 to β = − 1.60 \beta=-1.60 and G = 4.60 G=4.60 at k = 0.9 k=0.9 (Table 11 ). By contrast, input-connection ( weight_ih ) pruning flattens the Small LSTM spectrum to β = − 1.13 \beta=-1.13 and G = 3.10 G=3.10 at k = 0.9 k=0.9 (Table 12 ), whereas in the AWD-LSTM it causes an early steepening ( β = − 1.68 \beta=-1.68 , G = 5.05 G=5.05 at k = 0.4 k=0.4 ) followed by a partial reversal at k = 0.9 k=0.9 ( β = − 1.34 \beta=-1.34 , G = 4.17 G=4.17 ; Table 10 ).

blocks.zh: S5 详细数量性克隆分析,LSTM 路径不对称和代表性实例

blocks.en:
For Qwen 0.5B, baseline Cloze performance is strong: POS match = 65.0%, cosine similarity = 0.643 (Table 17 ).
Under MLP ablation, both metrics decline through k = 0.2 k=0.2 (POS 47.2%, cosine 0.421) and k = 0.3 k=0.3 (POS 35.2%, cosine 0.283), then collapse sharply at k = 0.4 k=0.4 (POS 8.8%, cosine 0.078) and k = 0.5 k=0.5 (POS 6.4%, cosine 0.042).
Under attention-head ablation, Qwen 0.5B retains substantially higher competence across the mid-range on the nominal- k k axis: at k = 0.4 k=0.4 , POS is 47.6% and cosine is 0.407 (more than fivefold higher than MLP ablation at the same nominal k k ), and at k = 0.5 k=0.5 , POS is 35.0% with a larger syntactic–semantic gap (cosine 0.198).
Qwen 1.8B shows the same contrast: from a baseline of POS = 64.0% and cosine = 0.663, MLP ablation drops to POS = 48.8% and cosine = 0.449 at k = 0.2 k=0.2 , 45.2% and 0.362 at k = 0.3 k=0.3 , 20.8% and 0.138 at k = 0.4 k=0.4 , and collapses to POS = 6.2% and cosine = 0.048 at k = 0.5 k=0.5 (Figure 5 , rows 2 and 3).
In contrast, Qwen 1.8B attention-head ablation retains POS = 59.9% and cosine = 0.606 at k = 0.2 k=0.2 , POS = 37.0% and cosine = 0.352 at k = 0.4 k=0.4 (about 1.8 × 1.8\times and 2.6 × 2.6\times the MLP values of 20.8% and 0.138), and still preserves POS = 42.0% and cosine = 0.319 at nominal k = 0.5 k=0.5 , outperforming MLP ablation by nearly sevenfold on both metrics at nominal k = 0.5 k=0.5 . Because nominal k = 0.5 k=0.5 removes 16.3 % 16.3\% (0.5B) and 16.6 % 16.6\% (1.8B) of non-embedding parameters under attention-head ablation versus 33.7 % 33.7\% and 33.4 % 33.4\% under MLP ablation (and 70.4 % 70.4\% and 72.7 % 72.7\% under LSTM whole-unit removal), at a matched parameter-removal fraction of ∼ 13.4 {\sim}13.4 – 20.2 % 20.2\% Qwen MLP ( k = 0.2 k=0.2 – 0.3 0.3 : POS 35.2 % 35.2\% – 48.8 % 48.8\% , cosine 0.283 0.283 – 0.449 0.449 ) and AWD-LSTM whole-unit removal ( k = 0.1 k=0.1 , 18.1 % 18.1\% removed: POS 53.0 % 53.0\% , cosine 0.393 0.393 ) match or exceed attention at k = 0.5 k=0.5 . Similarly, at ∼ 34 % {\sim}34\% of non-embedding parameters removed, AWD-LSTM whole-unit removal ( k = 0.2 k=0.2 , 34.5 % 34.5\% removed: POS 42.7 % 42.7\% , cosine 0.322 0.322 ) exceeds Qwen MLP at k = 0.5 k=0.5 (POS 6.2 6.2 – 6.4 % 6.4\% , cosine 0.042 0.042 – 0.048 0.048 ).

In the intact AWD-LSTM (baseline POS = 57.0%, cosine = 0.450; Figure 5 , row 1 right), whole-unit removal ( weight_ih + weight_hh + gate biases) degrades both POS match and cosine similarity in parallel without dissociation across mild-to-moderate damage: POS is 53.0% (cosine 0.393) at k = 0.1 k=0.1 , 42.7% (cosine 0.322) at k = 0.2 k=0.2 , and 28.4% (cosine 0.203) at k = 0.3 k=0.3 , before collapsing to 4.8% (cosine 0.074) at k = 0.4 k=0.4 , 2.2% (cosine 0.020) at k = 0.5 k=0.5 , 0.0% (cosine 0.008) at k = 0.6 k=0.6 , and 0.0% (cosine 0.000) for k ≥ 0.7 k\geq 0.7 (Table 17 ).
Our supplementary connection-pruning controls (Supplementary Figure 13 , row 2) isolate the two mechanisms behind this trajectory: under pure recurrent-connection ( weight_hh ) pruning, POS and cosine degrade gradually and in parallel across the entire sweep (POS 55.5%, cosine 0.417 at k = 0.2 k=0.2 ; 52.2%, 0.390 at k = 0.5 k=0.5 ; and 42.0%, 0.370 at k = 0.9 k=0.9 , preserving roughly three-quarters of baseline competence even at 90% recurrent pruning), whereas under pure input-connection ( weight_ih ) pruning, POS and cosine collapse steeply together (47.8% and 0.344 at k = 0.2 k=0.2 ; 34.4% and 0.244 at k = 0.3 k=0.3 ; 19.8% and 0.147 at k = 0.4 k=0.4 ; 5.2% and 0.040 at k = 0.5 k=0.5 ; and 1.6% and 0.047 at k = 0.9 k=0.9 ).

The Small LSTM exhibits the exact same pattern from a baseline of POS = 59.0% and cosine = 0.337 (Figure 5 , row 1 left, and Supplementary Figure 13 , row 1).
Under whole-unit removal, POS and cosine decline in parallel across k = 0.1 k=0.1 (41.6%, 0.279), k = 0.2 k=0.2 (23.6%, 0.177), and k = 0.3 k=0.3 (11.4%, 0.073), before collapsing to 1.6% (0.021) at k = 0.4 k=0.4 and 0.0% (0.000) for all k ≥ 0.5 k\geq 0.5 .
Under recurrent-connection ( weight_hh ) pruning alone, both POS and cosine decline gradually and in parallel across the full sweep (45.1% and 0.298 at k = 0.2 k=0.2 ; 34.0% and 0.251 at k = 0.5 k=0.5 ; and 20.4% and 0.170 at k = 0.9 k=0.9 ), whereas under input-connection ( weight_ih ) pruning alone, both metrics collapse rapidly (30.4% and 0.194 at k = 0.1 k=0.1 ; 7.3% and 0.051 at k = 0.2 k=0.2 ; and 0.0% and ≤ 0.002 \leq 0.002 for all k ≥ 0.3 k\geq 0.3 ).

In an LSTM, each hidden unit receives input from two additive sources at every time step: the input projection ( weight_ih ), which transforms the current token embedding x t x_{t} (or previous layer’s hidden state h t ( ℓ − 1 ) h_{t}^{(\ell-1)} ), and the recurrent projection ( weight_hh ), which propagates the previous time step’s hidden state h t − 1 ( ℓ ) h_{t-1}^{(\ell)} .
When weight_hh connections are pruned for a subset of units (Supplement control 1), those units still receive intact current-token projections via weight_ih : the feedforward pathway from the current token embedding through the LSTM gates to the tied output decoder remains unbroken, allowing the network to act as a local short-context predictor whose performance degrades gradually in proportion to the lost recurrent memory.
Conversely, when weight_ih is pruned (Supplement control 2), or when whole units are completely silenced in the main paper by zeroing both weight_ih and weight_hh across all layers (including outgoing columns feeding the next layer), the conduit through which current token information traverses the serial 3-layer stack is progressively narrowed and, at k ≥ 0.4 k\geq 0.4 (reaching 0.0 % 0.0\% POS by k = 0.5 k=0.5 – 0.6 0.6 ), starved of prompt information.
In the Transformer, Pre-Norm residual stream connections ( + + ) bypass each layer’s MLP and attention sub-blocks across all 24 layers, which may contribute to the early retention under attention-head ablation and to the abrupt threshold collapse under MLP ablation across k ∗ ≈ 0.3 k^{*}\approx 0.3 – 0.4 0.4 (after an early decline comparable to the LSTMs), whereas in the 3-layer LSTM, no residual stream bypasses the serial layer stack.

在变形器中,前诺姆残余流连接(++)绕过每层的MLP和所有24层的注意力小块,这可能有助于在注意力头膨胀下及早保留,并在MLP膨胀下突然发生阈值崩溃,跨越 k * * 0.3 k 大约 0.3 – 0.4 (在早期下降后与 LSTM 相比),而在3层的LSTM中,没有残余流绕过序列层堆.

blocks.en: • Comparison of intact and ablated models with post-stroke patient error distributions : In Figure 6 and Supplementary Table 20 , intact ( k = 0 k=0 ) Qwen 1.8B and Qwen 0.5B achieve 66.0 % 66.0\% and 64.0 % 64.0\% Correct, with 1.0 % 1.0\% No-response and 11.0 % 11.0\% and 9.0 % 9.0\% Semantic substitutions. When Correct is restricted to an exact top-1 match rather than top-5, first-trial rates are 42 % 42\% , 38 % 38\% , 7 % 7\% , and 0 % 0\% for the four intact baselines, and 22 % 22\% , 17 % 17\% , 37 % 37\% , 16 % 16\% , 1 % 1\% , and 1 % 1\% for the six unit-ablated conditions (listed in the row order of Table 4 ). At k = 0.2 k=0.2 across the 10 independent ablation trials ( N = 1,000 N=1{,}000 predictions per condition), Qwen 1.8B Correct rates bracket the 47.3 % 47.3\% PWA patient mean ( 42.1 % 42.1\% under MLP and 61.2 % 61.2\% under attention; 45 % 45\% and 61 % 61\% in the first trial). Under Qwen 1.8B MLP ablation, No-response errors jump from 1.0 % 1.0\% to 18.1 % 18.1\% (95% CI [ 3.0 3.0 , 33.2 33.2 ]; 16.7 % 16.7\% in Qwen 0.5B MLP), a wide interval that overlaps the 21.9 % 21.9\% patient rate. Unrelated word errors rise from 22.0 % 22.0\% to 27.9 % 27.9\% , while PNT Semantic paraphasias remain at 11.7 % 11.7\% under MLP versus 9.1 % 9.1\% under attention ( 18 % 18\% vs. 11 % 11\% in the first trial; patient reference 4.2 % 4.2\% ). By contrast, intact AWD-LSTM and Small LSTM start at 25.0 % 25.0\% and 4.0 % 4.0\% Correct at k = 0 k=0 and drop under whole-unit removal at k = 0.2 k=0.2 to 12.3 % 12.3\% and 0.6 % 0.6\% Correct across the 10 trials ( 9 % 9\% and 2 % 2\% in the first trial), with 62.4 % 62.4\% and 74.1 % 74.1\% Unrelated defaults and 9.8 % 9.8\% and 22.2 % 22.2\% No-response. Across the supplementary connection-pruning controls (Table 19 ), Correct rates range from 0.7 % 0.7\% to 20.2 % 20.2\% and No-response rates reach up to 55.5 % 55.5\% . • Null-corrected R 4 R_{4} and Jensen–Shannon divergence : At matched relative accuracy ( 0.80 0.80 ), the Jensen–Shannon divergence from the intact error distribution is larger in the Qwen unit-ablation pathways ( JS = 0.034 \mathrm{JS}=0.034 – 0.045 0.045 ; null-corrected Δ ​ JS = + 0.010 \Delta\mathrm{JS}=+0.010 to + 0.020 +0.020 ) than in LSTM whole-unit removal ( JS = 0.007 \mathrm{JS}=0.007 – 0.008 0.008 ; Δ ​ JS = + 0.002 \Delta\mathrm{JS}=+0.002 to + 0.003 +0.003 , Figure 4 ) or LSTM recurrent-connection pruning ( JS = 0.006 \mathrm{JS}=0.006 – 0.007 0.007 , Supplement S3 ). When trials are pooled across the shared transition range (without matching for relative accuracy or correcting for multiple comparisons), the normalised null-corrected shift ( R 4 obs − R 4 null ) / R 4 ​ ( 0 ) (R_{4}^{\mathrm{obs}}-R_{4}^{\mathrm{null}})/R_{4}(0) is more negative under MLP ablation than under attention-head ablation in both Qwen 0.5B ( − 0.0242 -0.0242 vs. − 0.0109 -0.0109 , two-sided permutation p < 10 − 4 p<10^{-4} ) and Qwen 1.8B ( − 0.0251 -0.0251 vs. − 0.0209 -0.0209 , p = 0.0238 p=0.0238 ). At a single interpolated accuracy slice ( 0.80 0.80 ), however, their 95% confidence intervals overlap (Supplement S3 ). • MLP ablation ↔ \leftrightarrow Wernicke-type aphasia : Across the 10 ablation trials at k = 0.2 k=0.2 (Table 4 ), Qwen 1.8B MLP retains 42.1 % 42.1\% [95% CI: 30.1 % , 54.1 % 30.1\%,54.1\% ] correct predictions and 27.2 % 27.2\% [ 21.7 % , 32.7 % 21.7\%,32.7\% ] content-word substitutions (in the first trial: 45 % 45\% correct, consisting of 22 % 22\% exact match plus 23 % 23\% top-5, and 38 % 38\% content substitutions). Its mean Brysbaert concreteness drop is Δ ​ Conc. = + 0.19 \Delta\text{Conc.}=+0.19 [ + 0.07 , + 0.30 +0.07,+0.30 ], which does not differ significantly from the intact baseline ( + 0.13 +0.13 ; difference + 0.06 +0.06 , 95% CI [ − 0.06 , + 0.17 ] [-0.06,+0.17] ; Supplement S7 ). For Qwen 0.5B MLP, the corresponding difference from intact is borderline ( + 0.29 +0.29 [ + 0.13 +0.13 , + 0.45 +0.45 ] vs. + 0.15 +0.15 intact; difference + 0.14 +0.14 , 95% CI [ − 0.02 , + 0.30 ] [-0.02,+0.30] ). On the PNT taxonomy (Figure 6 ; Supplementary Table 20 ), Qwen 1.8B MLP averages 11.7 % 11.7\% [ 9.2 % , 14.2 % 9.2\%,14.2\% ] Semantic errors across the 10 trials, maintaining its intact k = 0 k=0 rate of 11.0 % 11.0\% (difference + 0.70 +0.70 [ − 1.78 -1.78 , + 3.18 +3.18 ]). Over the same trials, Non-content responses rise by 23.7 23.7 [ 7.2 7.2 , 40.2 40.2 ] percentage points above intact and PNT No-responses rise by 17.1 17.1 [ 2.0 2.0 , 32.2 32.2 ] points (from 1.0 % 1.0\% to 18.1 % 18.1\% ; in Qwen 0.5B MLP, Non-content and No-response rise by 25.8 25.8 and 15.7 15.7 points). Compared with attention ablation ( 9.1 % 9.1\% [ 7.8 % , 10.4 % 7.8\%,10.4\% ] Semantic errors), Qwen 1.8B MLP shows a directional difference (two-sided permutation p = 0.0613 p=0.0613 , Holm-adjusted p = 0.1227 p=0.1227 ). In the first trial alone, Qwen 1.8B MLP produces 18 PNT Semantic paraphasias out of 38 content substitutions at θ s = 0.60 \theta_{s}=0.60 (rising to 27 of 38 at θ s = 0.50 \theta_{s}=0.50 ) and exceeds attention-head ablation at every similarity threshold θ s ∈ [ 0.50 , 0.80 ] \theta_{s}\in[0.50,0.80] in both Qwen 1.8B and Qwen 0.5B (Table 21 ). On the quantitative Cloze sweep (Table 2 ), Qwen 1.8B MLP retains moderate Cloze performance at k = 0.2 k=0.2 (POS 48.8 % 48.8\% , cosine 0.449 0.449 ) and k = 0.3 k=0.3 ( 45.2 % 45.2\% , 0.362 0.362 ) before collapsing at k = 0.5 k=0.5 to POS 6.2 % 6.2\% and cosine 0.048 0.048 (Qwen 0.5B MLP at k = 0.5 k=0.5 : POS 6.4 % 6.4\% , cosine 0.042 0.042 ), accompanied by the largest negative shift in null-corrected Δ ​ R 4 / R 4 ​ ( 0 ) \Delta R_{4}/R_{4}(0) ( − 0.0251 -0.0251 in Qwen 1.8B and − 0.0242 -0.0242 in Qwen 0.5B). • Attention-head ablation ↔ \leftrightarrow svPPA : At k = 0.2 k=0.2 , Qwen 1.8B attention ablation retains 61.2 % 61.2\% [ 59.4 % , 63.0 % 59.4\%,63.0\% ] correct predictions across the 10 trials ( 61 % 61\% in the first trial) and preserves Cloze POS at 59.9 % 59.9\% and cosine at 0.606 0.606 . (In Qwen 0.5B attention, the first trial is an atypically degraded outlier with 24 % 24\% Correct and 54 % 54\% Non-content, compared with the 10-trial means of 46.4 % 46.4\% and 24.5 % 24.5\% .) By nominal k = 0.5 k=0.5 , attention ablation removes 16.3 16.3 – 16.6 % 16.6\% of non-embedding weights (vs. 33.4 33.4 – 33.7 % 33.7\% under MLP ablation) and retains POS = 42.0 % =42.0\% and cosine = 0.319 =0.319 in Qwen 1.8B, compared with 6.2 % 6.2\% and 0.048 0.048 for MLP. Similarly, in Qwen 0.5B at nominal k = 0.5 k=0.5 , attention retains POS = 35.0 % =35.0\% and cosine = 0.198 =0.198 versus 6.4 % 6.4\% and 0.042 0.042 for MLP; when matched at ∼ 13 {\sim}13 – 20 % 20\% parameter removal (MLP k = 0.2 k=0.2 – 0.3 0.3 ), MLP retains POS 35.2 % 35.2\% – 48.8 % 48.8\% and cosine 0.283 0.283 – 0.449 0.449 (Table 2 ). Across the 10 trials at k = 0.2 k=0.2 (Table 4 ), the lemmatised Brysbaert concreteness drop under attention ablation rises above the intact baseline in Qwen 0.5B ( Δ ​ Conc. = + 0.43 \Delta\text{Conc.}=+0.43 [ 0.33 , 0.53 0.33,0.53 ] vs. + 0.15 +0.15 intact; difference + 0.28 +0.28 , 95% CI [ + 0.18 , + 0.38 ] [+0.18,+0.38] ; first trial + 0.60 +0.60 ) and is borderline in Qwen 1.8B ( Δ ​ Conc. = + 0.24 \Delta\text{Conc.}=+0.24 [ 0.13 , 0.34 0.13,0.34 ] vs. + 0.13 +0.13 intact; difference + 0.10 +0.10 , 95% CI [ + 0.00 , + 0.21 ] [+0.00,+0.21] ; first trial + 0.21 +0.21 ). Because these CIs treat the deterministic intact baseline as fixed, and the Qwen 0.5B MLP difference from intact ( + 0.14 +0.14 [ − 0.02 -0.02 , + 0.30 +0.30 ]) is of comparable size, concreteness alone does not cleanly separate the two pathways. LSTM recurrent-connection pruning also raises the concreteness drop significantly above its intact baseline ( + 0.14 +0.14 [ + 0.02 +0.02 , + 0.27 +0.27 ] in the Small LSTM and + 0.09 +0.09 [ + 0.02 +0.02 , + 0.16 +0.16 ] in the AWD-LSTM), showing that this shift is not unique to attention ablation; conversely, AWD-LSTM weight_hh pruning is the only condition with a significant rise in PNT Semantic errors ( + 2.6 +2.6 [ + 0.6 +0.6 , + 4.6 +4.6 ] points vs. intact). When we compare the two Qwen pathways directly across the 10 trials at k = 0.2 k=0.2 , point estimates shift in the clinically predicted direction in both models: PNT Semantic paraphasia rates are higher under MLP ( 11.7 % 11.7\% vs. 9.1 % 9.1\% in Qwen 1.8B, permutation p = 0.0613 p=0.0613 ; 9.9 % 9.9\% vs. 9.0 % 9.0\% in Qwen 0.5B, p = 0.6058 p=0.6058 ) and concreteness drops are larger under attention ( + 0.43 +0.43 vs. + 0.29 +0.29 in Qwen 0.5B, p = 0.1114 p=0.1114 ; + 0.24 +0.24 vs. + 0.19 +0.19 in Qwen 1.8B, p = 0.5019 p=0.5019 ). None of these direct error-type contrasts reaches statistical significance (Holm-adjusted p = 0.1227 p=0.1227 and 0.5019 0.5019 for the two Qwen 1.8B contrasts). These directional trends sit alongside the clear pathway separation in Cloze trajectories on the nominal- k k axis ( k = 0.3 k=0.3 – 0.6 0.6 , Figure 5 ) and in the pooled null-corrected R 4 R_{4} test ( p < 10 − 4 p<10^{-4} in Qwen 0.5B; p = 0.0238 p=0.0238 in Qwen 1.8B; not matched for relative accuracy). • LSTM whole-unit removal and pathway-connection controls ↔ \leftrightarrow Diffuse AD-type decline and late-stage collapse : Under whole-unit removal (Figures 2 a,b, 3 a,b, 4 , and 5 , row 1), next-token accuracy declines steadily across k ∈ [ 0 , 0.9 ] k\in[0,0.9] , retaining 82.2 % 82.2\% (Small LSTM) and 75.3 % 75.3\% (AWD-LSTM) of baseline at k = 0.2 k=0.2 , and 45.8 % 45.8\% and 34.4 % 34.4\% at k = 0.5 k=0.5 . Across the full sweep, raw R 4 R_{4} stays within 5.1 % 5.1\% (Small LSTM) and 7.7 % 7.7\% (AWD-LSTM) of baseline, and JS \mathrm{JS} at RelAcc = 0.80 \mathrm{RelAcc}=0.80 is only 0.007 0.007 – 0.008 0.008 . At k = 0.2 k=0.2 across the 10 trials (Table 4 ), AWD-LSTM whole-unit removal produces 12.3 % 12.3\% Correct predictions, 46.6 % 46.6\% Content substitutions, and 41.1 % 41.1\% Non-content responses ( Δ ​ Conc. = + 0.34 \Delta\text{Conc.}=+0.34 ), while Small LSTM whole-unit removal drops to 0.6 % 0.6\% Correct, 15.1 % 15.1\% Content substitutions, and 84.3 % 84.3\% Non-content ( Δ ​ Conc. = + 0.52 \Delta\text{Conc.}=+0.52 ). The supplementary connection-pruning controls (Table 19 ) separate the two mechanisms behind this behaviour. Pruning recurrent connections ( weight_hh ) alone preserves 48.3 % 48.3\% (Small LSTM) and 35.1 % 35.1\% (AWD-LSTM) of baseline accuracy even at k = 0.9 k=0.9 , keeps raw R 4 R_{4} within 3.4 % 3.4\% and 5.9 % 5.9\% of baseline ( JS = 0.006 \mathrm{JS}=0.006 – 0.007 0.007 at RelAcc = 0.80 \mathrm{RelAcc}=0.80 ), and reduces Cloze POS and cosine gradually through k = 0.9 k=0.9 (Small LSTM POS 59.0 % → 34.0 % → 20.4 % 59.0\%\to 34.0\%\to 20.4\% ; AWD-LSTM POS 57.0 % → 52.2 % → 42.0 % 57.0\%\to 52.2\%\to 42.0\% ; Table 17 ). blocks.en: Comparison of intact and ablated models with post-stroke patient error distributions : In Figure 6 and Supplementary Table 20 , intact ( k = 0 k=0 ) Qwen 1.8B and Qwen 0.5B achieve 66.0 % 66.0\% and 64.0 % 64.0\% Correct, with 1.0 % 1.0\% No-response and 11.0 % 11.0\% and 9.0 % 9.0\% Semantic substitutions. When Correct is restricted to an exact top-1 match rather than top-5, first-trial rates are 42 % 42\% , 38 % 38\% , 7 % 7\% , and 0 % 0\% for the four intact baselines, and 22 % 22\% , 17 % 17\% , 37 % 37\% , 16 % 16\% , 1 % 1\% , and 1 % 1\% for the six unit-ablated conditions (listed in the row order of Table 4 ). At k = 0.2 k=0.2 across the 10 independent ablation trials ( N = 1,000 N=1{,}000 predictions per condition), Qwen 1.8B Correct rates bracket the 47.3 % 47.3\% PWA patient mean ( 42.1 % 42.1\% under MLP and 61.2 % 61.2\% under attention; 45 % 45\% and 61 % 61\% in the first trial). Under Qwen 1.8B MLP ablation, No-response errors jump from 1.0 % 1.0\% to 18.1 % 18.1\% (95% CI [ 3.0 3.0 , 33.2 33.2 ]; 16.7 % 16.7\% in Qwen 0.5B MLP), a wide interval that overlaps the 21.9 % 21.9\% patient rate. Unrelated word errors rise from 22.0 % 22.0\% to 27.9 % 27.9\% , while PNT Semantic paraphasias remain at 11.7 % 11.7\% under MLP versus 9.1 % 9.1\% under attention ( 18 % 18\% vs. 11 % 11\% in the first trial; patient reference 4.2 % 4.2\% ). By contrast, intact AWD-LSTM and Small LSTM start at 25.0 % 25.0\% and 4.0 % 4.0\% Correct at k = 0 k=0 and drop under whole-unit removal at k = 0.2 k=0.2 to 12.3 % 12.3\% and 0.6 % 0.6\% Correct across the 10 trials ( 9 % 9\% and 2 % 2\% in the first trial), with 62.4 % 62.4\% and 74.1 % 74.1\% Unrelated defaults and 9.8 % 9.8\% and 22.2 % 22.2\% No-response. Across the supplementary connection-pruning controls (Table 19 ), Correct rates range from 0.7 % 0.7\% to 20.2 % 20.2\% and No-response rates reach up to 55.5 % 55.5\% .

blocks.en: MLP ablation ↔ \leftrightarrow Wernicke-type aphasia : Across the 10 ablation trials at k = 0.2 k=0.2 (Table 4 ), Qwen 1.8B MLP retains 42.1 % 42.1\% [95% CI: 30.1 % , 54.1 % 30.1\%,54.1\% ] correct predictions and 27.2 % 27.2\% [ 21.7 % , 32.7 % 21.7\%,32.7\% ] content-word substitutions (in the first trial: 45 % 45\% correct, consisting of 22 % 22\% exact match plus 23 % 23\% top-5, and 38 % 38\% content substitutions). Its mean Brysbaert concreteness drop is Δ ​ Conc. = + 0.19 \Delta\text{Conc.}=+0.19 [ + 0.07 , + 0.30 +0.07,+0.30 ], which does not differ significantly from the intact baseline ( + 0.13 +0.13 ; difference + 0.06 +0.06 , 95% CI [ − 0.06 , + 0.17 ] [-0.06,+0.17] ; Supplement S7 ). For Qwen 0.5B MLP, the corresponding difference from intact is borderline ( + 0.29 +0.29 [ + 0.13 +0.13 , + 0.45 +0.45 ] vs. + 0.15 +0.15 intact; difference + 0.14 +0.14 , 95% CI [ − 0.02 , + 0.30 ] [-0.02,+0.30] ). On the PNT taxonomy (Figure 6 ; Supplementary Table 20 ), Qwen 1.8B MLP averages 11.7 % 11.7\% [ 9.2 % , 14.2 % 9.2\%,14.2\% ] Semantic errors across the 10 trials, maintaining its intact k = 0 k=0 rate of 11.0 % 11.0\% (difference + 0.70 +0.70 [ − 1.78 -1.78 , + 3.18 +3.18 ]). S7 Concreteness Classification Methodology
blocks.zh: S7 具体程度分类方法

blocks.en:
To quantify whether content substitutions under ablation preserve the concreteness level of the target word (as in within-category paraphasia) or shift toward abstract vocabulary (as in generic defaulting), we use the concreteness norms of Brysbaert et al. [ Brysbaert et al., 2014 ] .
This dataset provides human-rated concreteness scores on a 1–5 scale (1 = highly abstract, 5 = highly concrete) for 39,954 English word lemmas, collected from over 4,000 participants via Amazon Mechanical Turk.
blocks.zh:
为了量化在减缩下的内容替代是保留目标词的混凝土水平(如类内抛物线),还是转向抽象词汇(如一般默认),我们使用Brysbaert等人的具体规范. [Brysbaert等人,2014].
这个数据集为39,954个英语单词lemmas提供了1–5级(1=高度抽象,5=高度混凝土)的人类评级混凝土分数,通过亚马逊机械特克从4000多名参与者那里收集.

blocks.en:
For each content word substitution (i.e., predictions classified as neither correct, non-content, nor function words), we compute the concreteness drop : Δ ​ Conc. = Conc ​ ( target ) − Conc ​ ( prediction ) \Delta\text{Conc.}=\text{Conc}(\text{target})-\text{Conc}(\text{prediction}) .
Words are looked up first in surface form and then via WordNet lemmatisation (across noun, verb, adjective, and adverb parts of speech) so that regular inflected forms (such as vegetables → \to vegetable , 4.89, or walked → \to walk , 4.07) are scored rather than discarded.
A positive value indicates that the prediction is more abstract than the target (loss of specificity); a value near zero indicates that the prediction preserves the target’s concreteness level (consistent with within-category substitution); a negative value indicates a shift toward more concrete vocabulary.
blocks.zh:
对于每个内容单词替换(即被分类为既不正确,又不包含内容,也不包含函数单词的预测),我们计算混凝土下降: \\ Conc. = Conc(目标) – Conc(预测)\Delta\text{Conc.\text{Conc}(\text{目标})\text{Conc}(\text{port{president}).
单词首先以表面形式,然后通过WordNet lemmatisation(介于名词,动词,形容词和语音的副词部分)来查看,这样,普通的反射形式(如蔬菜 ~\to蔬菜 ,4.89,或步行 ~\步行 ,4.07)会被打分而不是丢弃.
一个正值表示预测比目标更抽象(丧失特异性);一个接近零值表示预测保持目标的具体程度水平(与类内替代一致);一个负值表示向更具体词汇转变.

blocks.en: S8 Re-coding into the Philadelphia Naming Test Taxonomy
blocks.zh: S8 重新编码为费城命名测试分类学

blocks.en:
The three-way classification of Table 4 (Correct / Content substitution / Non-content) was designed for this study and does not correspond to any coding scheme in the clinical literature, which prevents direct numerical comparison with published patient data.
We therefore re-coded the same predictions into the seven-category taxonomy conventionally applied to the Philadelphia Naming Test [ Roach et al., 1996 , Mirman et al., 2010 ] , as visualised in Figure 6 in Section 2.5 and tabulated in Supplementary Table 20 below (and Supplementary Table 19 for the LSTM connection-pruning controls).
We evaluate both the full 10-trial evaluation at k = 0.2 k=0.2 ( 1,000 1{,}000 predictions per condition across 10 independent ablation trials, reported in Table 4 , Figure 6 , and Supplementary Tables 19 and 20 ) and the individual predictions from the first ablation trial listed in Supplements S10 – S13 (100 prompts for each of the six primary unit-level ablation conditions and four LSTM connection-pruning controls at k = 0.2 k=0.2 , together with the four undamaged baselines: 14 tables × \times 100 prompts = 1,400 =1{,}400 predictions).
Each record consists of the prompt, the expected target, the model’s top-1 prediction, and the top-5 candidate list.

因此,我们把同样的预测重新编码为传统上适用于费城命名试验的七类分类法[Roach等人,1996年,Mirman等人,2010年],如图6第2.5节所示,并列于下文补充表20(以及LSTM连接推算控制的补充表19)。
我们评价了表4、图6和补充表19和20中报告的10次独立断裂试验中的10次全面审判评价为k=0.2k=0.2(1,000 1{,} 000个条件的预测为每次),以及S10号补编-S13号所列第一次断裂试验中的个别预测(K=0.2k=0.2k=0.2,4个LSTM连接断裂控制为每次,加上4个未受损基线:14个表xx100次断裂=1400=1{,400个预测)。

blocks.en:
In clinical neuropsychology, a patient’s spoken responses on the Philadelphia Naming Test are categorized by expert examiners based on whether an error shares the target’s semantic category, sound structure, both, or neither [ Roach et al., 1996 , Mirman et al., 2010 ] .
To compare computational model predictions directly against clinical patient distributions without subjective scoring bias or manual labeling inconsistency, we operationalize the clinical diagnostic criteria into a fully automatic, deterministic decision procedure.
The procedure evaluates each (target, prediction) pair along the two primary linguistic dimensions defining aphasic speech errors: semantic category relatedness ( s s ) and phonological similarity ( p p ).
blocks.zh:
在临床神经心理学中,一位患者在费城命名测试中的口述反应被专家检查者根据一个错误是否与目标语义类别,声音结构相同而加以分类,两者均相同,或者两者都不相同[Roach等人,1996年,Mirman等人,2010年].
为了将计算模型预测直接与临床病人分布进行比较,而不会主观的评分偏差或手动标注不一致,我们把临床诊断标准应用为一个完全自动的,决定性的决定程序.
该程序沿界定语义性语音错误的两个主要语言维度(目标,预测)对每一对进行评价:语义类关联性(s s)和声学相似性(p.

blocks.en:
Semantic relatedness, denoted s ∈ [ 0 , 1 ] s\in[0,1] , is the maximum Wu–Palmer taxonomy similarity in WordNet [ Fellbaum, 1998 ] over synset pairs restricted to the target’s annotated part of speech, measuring conceptual proximity in the category hierarchy. Because WordNet organises nouns and verbs into hypernym trees but represents adjectives and adverbs as satellite clusters without hypernym paths, Wu–Palmer similarity returns s = 0 s=0 for all non-synonymous adjective and adverb pairs ( s = 1 s=1 only when both words share an exact synset). Consequently, across the 27 adjective and adverb prompts (27% of the battery), non-synonymous substitutions cannot be coded as Semantic or Mixed and fall into Unrelated (or Formal). Closed-class predictions are not eligible to count as semantic paraphasias, since WordNet assigns them senses that yield spuriously high similarity.
We use WordNet category similarity rather than word-embedding cosine because clinical semantic paraphasia means substituting a word from the same category (such as “river” or “bay” for “ocean”), whereas embedding cosine also rewards words that merely appear in similar contexts (such as “boat” for “ocean”).
Phonological similarity, denoted p ∈ [ 0 , 1 ] p\in[0,1] , measures normalized phonemic overlap: p = 1 − d / max ⁡ ( | a | , | b | ) p=1-d/\max(|a|,|b|) , where a a and b b are phoneme sequences from the CMU Pronouncing Dictionary (with lexical stress removed), d d is the Levenshtein edit distance between them, and | a | , | b | |a|,|b| are sequence lengths.
A pair is treated as phonologically related only if p ≥ θ p p\geq\theta_{p} and the two words share their initial phoneme, which prevents unrelated short words from registering as formal errors.
For example, substituting “bowl” (/B OW L/) for target “ball” (/B AO L/) alters only one vowel out of three phonemes ( d = 1 d=1 , max ⁡ ( | a | , | b | ) = 3 \max(|a|,|b|)=3 ), giving p = 1 − 1 / 3 = 0.67 p=1-1/3=0.67 . Because p ≥ θ p = 0.50 p\geq\theta_{p}=0.50 and both share the initial phoneme /B/, this substitution satisfies the phonological criterion.

blocks.en:
Four caveats apply when comparing our Cloze predictions with clinical PNT naming data.
First, clinical PNT responses come from picture naming, where a stimulus picture specifies a single target word. Our Cloze prompts provide a sentence context that allows several plausible continuations. As a result, predictions that fit the sentence context without matching the target or its WordNet category are coded as Unrelated. This property of the elicitation task (rather than of the models themselves) explains why Unrelated responses are much more frequent in our models ( 25.6 25.6 – 81.5 % 81.5\% across the 10 ablation trials; 23 23 – 84 % 84\% in the first trial) than in patients ( 6.1 % 6.1\% ).
Second, the patient reference pools data across severity levels and aphasia subtypes, so it shows whether ablated models fall within the overall aphasic range rather than whether a specific ablation matches a specific syndrome.
Third, the two studies use different scoring instruments: our deterministic WordNet/CMUdict rules versus a classifier trained on speech-language pathologist annotations, so part of the difference reflects measurement rather than model behaviour.
Fourth, WordNet Wu–Palmer similarity is relatively high for pairs of abstract nouns because abstract concepts sit near the top of the WordNet hierarchy, whereas for adjectives and adverbs ( 27 % 27\% of the prompts) WordNet lacks hypernym trees and returns s = 0 s=0 for all non-synonymous pairs. Consequently, abstract noun pairs slightly inflate the Semantic count near the θ s = 0.60 \theta_{s}=0.60 cutoff. In the first ablation trial, 34 of 639 classified real-word responses across the 1,000 1{,}000 ablated predictions fall within 0.05 0.05 of θ s = 0.60 \theta_{s}=0.60 (see Supplementary Table 21 for the full θ s ∈ [ 0.50 , 0.80 ] \theta_{s}\in[0.50,0.80] sweep).
blocks.zh:
在将我们的克洛兹预测与临床的PNT命名数据进行比较时,适用了四个警告.
首先,临床的PNT反应来自图片命名,其中刺激图片指定了一个单一的目标词. 我们的Cloze提示提供了一种句子上下文,允许几种可信的续作. 因此,与句子上下文不匹配的目标或其WordNet类的预测被编码为无关联. 诱导任务(而不是模型本身)的这一属性解释了为何在我们的模式中,无关的反应比病人(6.1 % )频繁得多(在10次禁欲试验中,25.6 25.6 — — 81.5 % — — 81.5);在第一次试验中,23 – 84% — — 84 % — )。
第二,患者参考集合了跨重度水平和aphasia亚型的数据,因此它显示了被消化的模型是否属于整体的aphasic范围,而不是一个特定的衰竭是否与一个特定的综合征相匹配.
第三,这两项研究使用不同的评分工具:我们的定型WordNet/CMUdict规则与接受语言病理学说明培训的分类器,因此部分差异反映的是测量而不是模型行为.

blocks.en: To determine how much of the post-lesion behaviour reflects pre-existing structural reserve versus gradient-based weight adaptation, we compare up to four fine-tuning regimes across the full damage sweep k ∈ { 0.0 , 0.1 , … , 0.9 } k\in\{0.0,0.1,\ldots,0.9\} across both recurrent architectures (Small LSTM and AWD-LSTM) and the Transformer models (Qwen 0.5B across both pathways and Qwen 1.8B MLP): 1. none : zero fine-tuning steps ( ‖ Δ ​ θ ‖ 2 = 0 \|\Delta\theta\|_{2}=0 ), measuring pure pre-existing architectural redundancy immediately after zeroing the ablated weights. 2. weak (default main-paper protocol): brief fixed-step SGD without momentum ( lr = 10 − 3 \mathrm{lr}=10^{-3} , gradient clipping 0.25 0.25 ; 40 BPTT steps for Small LSTM and 50 BPTT steps for AWD-LSTM, and 62 weight updates for Qwen accumulating gradients over 8 stories across 500 TinyStories passages with per-passage gradient clipping to 0.25 0.25 ), producing small, strictly local parameter adjustments ( ‖ Δ ​ θ ‖ 2 ≈ 0.0016 \|\Delta\theta\|_{2}\approx 0.0016 – 0.0094 0.0094 in Small LSTM, 0.0018 0.0018 – 0.0119 0.0119 in AWD-LSTM, 0.003 0.003 – 0.010 0.010 in Qwen 0.5B, and 0.004 0.004 – 0.009 0.009 in Qwen 1.8B MLP). 3. strong : 500 gradient steps of AdamW ( lr = 10 − 4 \mathrm{lr}=10^{-4} , gradient clipping 1.0 1.0 ) on TinyStories ( ‖ Δ ​ θ ‖ 2 ≈ 46 \|\Delta\theta\|_{2}\approx 46 – 80 80 in Small LSTM [ 3.0 3.0 – 77 77 under weight_ih ], 73 73 – 176 176 in AWD-LSTM, 87 87 – 116 116 in Qwen 0.5B, and 72 72 – 78 78 in Qwen 1.8B MLP for k ≤ 0.2 k\leq 0.2 ), representing an upper bound of global weight re-optimisation across all surviving parameters. 4. strong_wt103 (Small LSTM and AWD-LSTM): 500 gradient steps of AdamW ( lr = 10 − 4 \mathrm{lr}=10^{-4} , gradient clipping 1.0 1.0 ) on in-domain WikiText-103 ( ‖ Δ ​ θ ‖ 2 ≈ 34 \|\Delta\theta\|_{2}\approx 34 – 67 67 in Small LSTM [ 3.4 3.4 – 70 70 under weight_ih ] and 68 68 – 168 168 in AWD-LSTM), testing whether prolonged in-domain retraining induces a buffered plateau in recurrent architectures.

blocks.en: Across all models, this comparison establishes three main findings (Supplementary Figures 14 – 16 ). First, zero fine-tuning ( none ) and brief local SGD ( weak ) produce similar curve shapes: even at ‖ Δ ​ θ ‖ 2 = 0 \|\Delta\theta\|_{2}=0 , Qwen shows a late threshold collapse under MLP ablation and an early plateau under attention ablation (scoring 2 ​ – ​ 6 2\text{--}6 percentage points lower in raw accuracy than weak , whereas none and weak coincide in the LSTMs). Second, in the LSTMs, even 500 steps of in-domain AdamW retraining ( strong_wt103 ) lift overall accuracy at high k k without inducing a buffered plateau. Third, in the Transformers, 500 steps of global AdamW ( strong ) act as wholesale network retraining across surviving layers (recovering 86 % ​ – ​ 99 % 86\%\text{--}99\% of baseline accuracy even at k = 0.9 k=0.9 ), which is why we use brief local SGD ( weak ) as our primary protocol.
blocks.zh: 在所有模式中,这一比较确立了三个主要结果(补充图14至16)。 首先,零微调(无)和简短的局部 SGD(弱)产生相似的曲线形状:即使在 QQ = QQ = 0. Delta\theta\2\0时, Quen 显示在 MLP 衰减 和 注意力衰减 下的早期高原(得分 2–6 2\text{-} ) 下,原始精度比弱低6个百分点,而在 LSTM 中则没有和弱的重合 。 其次,在LSTMs中,甚至有500步的域内亚当W再培训(strong_wt103)在高kk提升整体精度,而不会诱导缓冲高原. 第三,在变形器中,500个步骤的全球AdamW(强)在生存层中起到批发网络再培训的作用(恢复86 % —99 % 86\%\text{-}99\%基线精度,甚至以k=0.9 k=0.9),这就是为什么我们使用简短的本地SGD(弱)作为我们的主要协议。

blocks.en: Supplementary Figures 14 and 15 show all three ablation modes ( weight_hh recurrent connections, weight_ih input connections, and weight_ih + weight_hh whole-unit removal) for the Small LSTM and the pretrained AWD-LSTM, respectively. In both recurrent models and across all three ablation modes, the none and weak curves are virtually identical. In the Small LSTM (baseline 27.5 % 27.5\% ), whole-unit accuracy is 22.6 % 22.6\% vs. 22.6 % 22.6\% at k = 0.2 k=0.2 and 12.6 % 12.6\% vs. 12.6 % 12.6\% at k = 0.5 k=0.5 (and under weight_hh pruning, 21.3 % 21.3\% vs. 21.3 % 21.3\% at k = 0.2 k=0.2 and 15.9 % 15.9\% vs. 15.9 % 15.9\% at k = 0.5 k=0.5 ). In the AWD-LSTM (baseline 38.1 % 38.1\% ), whole-unit accuracy is 28.7 % 28.7\% vs. 28.7 % 28.7\% at k = 0.2 k=0.2 and 13.1 % 13.1\% vs. 13.1 % 13.1\% at k = 0.5 k=0.5 (and under weight_hh pruning, 33.0 % 33.0\% vs. 33.0 % 33.0\% at k = 0.2 k=0.2 and 21.9 % 21.9\% vs. 21.9 % 21.9\% at k = 0.5 k=0.5 ). Prolonged 500-step AdamW retraining on in-domain WikiText-103 ( strong_wt103 ) lifts accuracy at higher damage levels in both LSTMs. In the Small LSTM ( k = 0 k=0 baseline 27.6 % 27.6\% ), whole-unit accuracy at k = 0.5 k=0.5 rises from 12.6 % 12.6\% under none / weak to 17.4 % 17.4\% ( 62.9 % 62.9\% of baseline), and weight_hh accuracy rises from 15.9 % 15.9\% to 21.0 % 21.0\% ( 76.0 % 76.0\% ). In the AWD-LSTM, the k = 0 k=0 baseline falls slightly from 38.05 % 38.05\% to 37.02 % 37.02\% , while at k = 0.5 k=0.5 whole-unit accuracy rises from 13.1 % 13.1\% to 20.5 % 20.5\% and weight_hh accuracy rises from 21.9 % 21.9\% to 26.9 % 26.9\% . Even so, the whole-unit and recurrent trajectories in both LSTMs remain smooth and gradual without any buffered plateau. Because 40–50 steps of clipped SGD at lr = 10 − 3 \mathrm{lr}=10^{-3} on out-of-domain TinyStories move the LSTM weights by only ‖ Δ ​ θ ‖ 2 ≤ 0.0119 \|\Delta\theta\|_{2}\leq 0.0119 (relative change ∼ 10 − 5 {\sim}10^{-5} ), the LSTM weak arm leaves WikiText-2 accuracy unchanged and is effectively equivalent to none . By contrast, 500 steps of AdamW on the same TinyStories tensor in the strong arm do shift WikiText-2 accuracy (for example, lifting Small LSTM weight_ih accuracy at k = 0.2 k=0.2 from 3.7 % 3.7\% to 15.4 % 15.4\% ). Thus, the LSTM and Qwen weak arms are not symmetric.

blocks.en: Supplementary Figure 16 shows the two Qwen 0.5B pathways (MLP neuron removal and attention-head removal). With zero fine-tuning ( none ), the late threshold collapse is already present, although MLP retention at mild damage is lower than for Small LSTM whole-unit removal under the same arm ( 92.8 % 92.8\% and 82.2 % 82.2\% at k = 0.1 k=0.1 and 0.2 0.2 ). Specifically, Qwen 0.5B retains 85.3 % 85.3\% (MLP, 44.0 % 44.0\% raw) and 96.4 % 96.4\% (Attention, 49.7 % 49.7\% raw) of its unadapted k = 0 k=0 baseline ( 51.5 % 51.5\% ) at k = 0.1 k=0.1 , and 66.1 % 66.1\% (MLP, 34.1 % 34.1\% raw) and 81.7 % 81.7\% (Attention, 42.1 % 42.1\% raw) at k = 0.2 k=0.2 , before dropping steeply to 17.1 % 17.1\% ( 8.8 % 8.8\% raw) at k = 0.4 k=0.4 under MLP ablation and to the same level at k = 0.5 k=0.5 under attention ablation. Brief local SGD ( weak ) shifts accuracy modestly upward (for example, MLP at k = 0.2 k=0.2 : 34.1 % → 37.9 % 34.1\%\to 37.9\% ; at k = 0.3 k=0.3 : 24.9 % → 30.4 % 24.9\%\to 30.4\% ) while preserving the sharp cliff at k ≥ 0.4 k\geq 0.4 . The larger Qwen 1.8B MLP pathway exhibits the same pattern. With zero fine-tuning ( none , k = 0 k=0 baseline 50.6 % 50.6\% ), accuracy remains at 48.5 % 48.5\% ( 96.0 % 96.0\% of baseline) at k = 0.1 k=0.1 , 41.5 % 41.5\% ( 82.1 % 82.1\% ) at k = 0.2 k=0.2 , and 27.4 % 27.4\% ( 54.2 % 54.2\% ) at k = 0.3 k=0.3 , then drops sharply to 8.9 % 8.9\% ( 17.6 % 17.6\% ) at k = 0.4 k=0.4 and 7.5 % 7.5\% ( 14.8 % 14.8\% ) at k = 0.5 k=0.5 . This closely matches the weak trajectory ( 51.1 % 51.1\% [ 93.5 % 93.5\% ] at k = 0.1 k=0.1 , 44.8 % 44.8\% [ 82.0 % 82.0\% ] at k = 0.2 k=0.2 , and 12.9 % 12.9\% [ 23.5 % 23.5\% ] at k = 0.4 k=0.4 ). By contrast, 500 steps of AdamW ( strong , ‖ Δ ​ θ ‖ 2 ≈ 87 \|\Delta\theta\|_{2}\approx 87 – 116 116 in Qwen 0.5B and 72 72 – 78 78 in Qwen 1.8B MLP for k ≤ 0.2 k\leq 0.2 ) globally re-optimise the surviving residual stream and un-lesioned layers to bypass the ablated sub-blocks almost completely. This restores Qwen 0.5B accuracy to 98.0 % 98.0\% of baseline ( 52.2 % 52.2\% raw) at k = 0.5 k=0.5 and 86.0 % 86.0\% ( 45.8 % 45.8\% raw) at k = 0.9 k=0.9 under MLP ablation, and to 95.9 % 95.9\% – 99.0 % 99.0\% ( 51.1 % 51.1\% – 52.7 % 52.7\% raw) across all k ∈ [ 0.1 , 0.9 ] k\in[0.1,0.9] under attention ablation. In Qwen 1.8B MLP, it restores accuracy to 51.2 % 51.2\% raw ( 103.1 % 103.1\% of the 49.7 % 49.7\% strong k = 0 k=0 baseline) at k = 0.1 k=0.1 and 50.7 % 50.7\% raw ( 102.1 % 102.1\% ) at k = 0.2 k=0.2 . For Qwen 1.8B, the 500-step strong MLP sweep beyond k = 0.2 k=0.2 and the none / strong attention sweeps were omitted due to compute constraints, while the complete 10-point k ∈ [ 0 , 0.9 ] k\in[0,0.9] sweep across all three arms in Qwen 0.5B and across none / weak in Qwen 1.8B MLP is reported above.
